newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blue chips end lower ahead of key jobs report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blue chips end lower ahead of key jobs report.

text.p: The Dow industrials retreated back below the 7000 level on Thursday as investors took profits from the market's sizzling advance and braced for a critical payroll and wage report due Friday morning.
The Dow fell 33 points to close unofficially at 6976, snapping a three-session winning streak for the blue-chip average.
The broader market enjoyed a solid day, however. Advancing issues outpaced decliners on the major exchanges, with small cap and tech stocks showing particular strength.
The performance encouraged analysts, who have warily watched the broad market fail to follow the lead set by the Dow during its powerful recovery from a monthlong correction.

"The recovery, even in the S&P 500, has really been led by 10 or 15 companies," said Jack Shaughnessy, director of research at Advest. "You really want many more stocks participating to have a sustainable advance."
Analysts said the Dow's pause was almost inevitable on the day before the monthly U.S. wage and payrolls data, one of the very few reports that draw almost universal attention on Wall Street.

Last summer, a stronger-than-expected payroll report triggered the initial sell-off in what proved to be a steep decline. Analysts said a surprise on Friday, either way, could easily lead to another tempestuous session.
"Could we get another 100-point-plus day either way tomorrow? Absolutely," said Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management.

The balance of data this week by and large has proved reassuring to investors, showing a very strong economy without inflation -- the so-called "Goldilocks" economy because its pace is believed to be neither too hot nor too cold.

"For the most part, the inflation watch is focused on the wages," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "The other side of the issue is how do we relate wage increases to productivity growth."
"For now, the market seems comfortable, because we're seeing fast growth but we're not seeing inflation accelerate," he said.

In individual issues, Aames Financial Corp tumbled 3-1/8 to 12-1/4. Late Wednesday, the mortgage lender warned that a plan to review the pricing of loans made by third party brokers could hurt its future earnings.

Adobe Systems Inc jumped 2-5/8 to 41-3/4, a day after Standard & Poor's announced the software company would fill a vacancy in its S&P 500 Index. The index, a benchmark for large-cap equities, is used to set investment allocations at many mutual funds.
Adobe had been a component of S&P's MidCap 400 Index. Its replacement there, Hillenbrand Industries Inc, gained 2-3/8 to 45-3/8. Both changes take effect next Monday.
Hallwood Group Inc rose 2-5/8 to 27-1/8. The diversified holding company said it planned to buy back 19.1 percent of its shares for $27.50 each in a self-tender.
The S&P 500 index fell 2.81 points to 798.53.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 9.74 points to 1270.50.
The Russell 2000 index rose 2.66 points to 345.66.
